text:
anya: Heads up — we saw a sudden drop in prefix cache hit-rate on a dedicated canary and a corresponding tail-latency bump. CC @sam @kevin

sam: Which canary/cluster?

anya: ded-23-eu, rolled yesterday ~09:12 UTC. hit-rate for convo-prefix keys fell from ~82% -> ~46% during the window, p95 token latency up ~28%.

kevin: Do you have the metric slice?

anya: Paste from metrics:```
prefix_cache.hitrate{env="ded23",workload="chat"} 2025-11-09T09:00..11:00
09:00 avg: 82.1% -> 09:20 avg: 45.8%
p50_latency: 16ms -> 19ms
p95_latency: 78ms -> 100ms
```

marta: Any recent changes to key normalization or kernel-selection heuristics?

kevin: Yes — PR #4127 changed our prompt normalization (we disabled aggressive stripping) and introduced stable_hash_v2. Also a batching heuristic tweak: prefer_coalesce=true for short sequences.

sam: stable_hash_v2 tightened whitespace handling, right? could create higher cardinality if invisible chars or minor markup changed.

anya: I grabbed a couple of sample prefixes from the canary traces:
```
System priming: "###Instructions
Keep it short"
User message: "Hello"
Key_v1: hash("###Instructions
Keep it short|Hello")
Key_v2: hash("###Instructions\u200b
Keep it short|Hello")  # note zero-width space in second
```

kevin: That zero-width-char looks like the culprit. Devex sanitizer change merged yesterday may have started injecting soft-breaks for some markup.

marta: Also interesting: kernel selection flipped around 09:15 — short sequences moved from fast_f32 -> fallback_quant. That increases latency and may interact with cache tagging.

sam: How does kernel selection change hit-rate?

kevin: We currently tag cache keys with a runtime fingerprint (kernel_id + quant_state) to avoid serving incompatible KV caches across kernel variants. So if kernel_id flips, the keys are considered different even if the prompt is identical.

anya: So sanitizer change + kernel-tagging = high churn and eviction. That explains the drop. :facepalm: 

sam: Short-term mitigation idea: decouple prefix keying from kernel_id for very short priming sequences (len<64). Risk: if quant path changes semantics we could return incompatible cache entries. Need a coherence test.

marta: Proposed immediate plan:
- revert sanitizer patch (hotfix)
- introduce a runtime flag to use "len<64" prefix_key_mode that omits kernel tag (flag: prefix_key_strict=false) and enable on canary only
- run 5% traffic canary and monitor hit-rate, tail latency, and KV coherency tests
- longer term: canonicalize invisible chars at prompt ingestion and remove kernel in key where safe

kevin: I'll open rollback PR + flag now. Hotfix ETA ~10m.

anya: Quick profiler snapshot we captured:```
before (baseline): prefix-hit=82%, tokens/sec=12.4k, tail-rpc=120ms
after (post-rollout): prefix-hit=46%, tokens/sec=8.1k, tail-rpc=152ms
kernel-flip rate: 14% -> 62%
```

sam: Any eval or quality regressions from canary?

marta: Ran a small eval harness (1000 prompts) — semantic outputs match baseline, no regression alerts. This looks purely cost/latency.

anya: I'll trigger rollback and enable the len<64 key mode in canary. Will post metrics once 5% flows through.

kevin: PRs opened: #4190 (revert sanitizer), #4191 (prefix_key_len_flag). Starting canary 5% now.

perf-bot: Canary deployment started: ded-23-eu, split=5%. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/prefix-cache/overview

sam: I'll add temporary alert: prefix_cache.hitrate < 60% for ded-23 -> page on breach.

anya: Thanks — if hit-rate recovers we'll iterate on two long-term options: (A) omit kernel tag for prefix-only cache with stricter coherence testing, (B) keep tag but aggressively canonicalize inputs upstream (strip invisible chars, normalize unicode).

kevin: I'll also add a small unit test for zero-width + sanitizer to prevent future merges.

anya: TL;DR — root cause = invisible-char normalization change + kernel-tagged keys. Hotfix + feature-flagged mitigation rolling; monitoring in flight.

perf-bot: Canary metrics (30m): hit-rate rising to 78% on the flagged path, tail latency trending back down.

marta: Nice, please note results in the rollout doc and we can schedule a sticky follow-up to ship canonicalization and stronger unit tests.
